title: Platform systems & services — runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates the eng-platform team’s canonical references for platform systems and services: operational runbooks, how-tos, dashboards & alerts, retrospectives, and the 12–18 month roadmap. It is the single source of truth for on-call engineers and product/infra stakeholders for standard operating procedures, ownership, and deployment guidance.

Goals:
- Provide clear operational runbooks for production services (platform-api, telemetry-ingest, config-service, console-web, batch-worker).
- Standardize dashboards and alert thresholds to reduce noise and improve meantime-to-resolution (MTTR).
- Capture retrospectives and action items from major incidents and game-days.
- Maintain a living roadmap with owners and major milestones.

Owners and contact list:
- Platform Systems & Services: eng-platform (primary) — owner: Avery Chen (eng lead)
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall (pager duty) — primary escalation: Diego Morales, secondary: Priya Nair
- Observability & Telemetry: telemetry-team — slack #telemetry-ops

Key services (short descriptions):
- platform-api: public/internal gateway that routes user inference/control-plane requests. Handles auth, routing, and request shaping.
- telemetry-ingest: high-throughput consumer for usage events, metrics enrichment, and forwarding to metrics and logs pipelines.
- config-service: centralized runtime config and feature-flag store used by all platform components.
- console-web: customer-facing console; static frontend + backend for dashboarding and query APIs.
- batch-worker: asynchronous job workers for background tasks (cleanup, compaction, rollout orchestration).

SLOs (summary):
- platform-api latency: 99th percentile p99 < 200ms for control-plane routes, p95 < 120ms.
- request success rate: 99.9% availability (monthly).
- telemetry-ingest ingestion lag: 99th percentile < 15s.
- console-web page load: p95 < 1.5s.

Dashboards (what to look at):
- Platform Overview dashboard (owner: eng-platform): service health, 5xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, request rate, error budget burn chart.
- Telemetry Pipeline dashboard (owner: telemetry): ingestion lag histogram, consumer lag per partition, throughput (events/sec), processing error rate.
- Infrastructure Utilization (owner: eng-infra): GPU node utilization, memory pressure, disk IO, node restart trends.
- Cost & Batching dashboard (owner: infra-economics): tokens/second, batching efficiency, cache hit rate, per-token cost estimate.

Standard alerting thresholds (apply to service dashboards):
| Alert name | Trigger | Severity | Runbook | Owner |
|-----------|---------|----------|---------|-------|
| platform-api-5xx-rate | > 0.5% 5xx over 5m and > 5rps | P1 | See section: Runbook — platform-api 5xx | oncall/platform |
| platform-api-latency-p99 | p99 > 400ms for 10m | P1 | Runbook: latency degradation | oncall/platform |
| telemetry-ingest-lag-high | ingestion lag p99 > 30s for 5m | P2 | Runbook: consumer lag | telemetry |
| config-service-unavailable | service check fails 3x in 2m | P1 | Runbook: config-service outage | platform |
| console-web-error-rate | error rate > 1% and >10rps for 5m | P2 | Runbook: console frontend errors | web |

Runbooks (quick links & playbook snippets):
1) platform-api 5xx spike (P1)
   - Page: platform-oncall group
   - Immediate checks (first 5 min):
     1. Confirm alert in Grafana/Alertmanager and check for related alerts (latency, infra).
     2. Check platform-api pods: kubectl get pods -n platform | grep platform-api — look for CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled.
     3. Review recent deploys: gitops/deploy history, CI pipeline: last 30 minutes.
     4. Check upstream model/node pool health: gpu-fleet dashboard and node agent logs.
   - If cause is increased load: enable emergency rate-limiting rule in API gateway (instructions below) and scale deployment (kubectl scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=<n>).
   - If cause is code regression: roll back to previous revision via deploy pipeline (tags: production-rollback).
   - Post-incident: open incident doc, tag with root_cause, and schedule a follow-up retro.

2) Telemetry consumer lag (P2)
   - Verify consumer group offsets (kafka-consumer-groups.sh) and check for GC/CPU saturation on consumers.
   - If consumer stuck: restart consumer pod with graceful drain, ensure rebalancing does not cause further lag.

Common commands and snippets:
- Check pods (namespace): kubectl get pods -n platform -o wide
- Inspect logs: kubectl logs -n platform <pod> -c app --since=15m | tail -n 200
- Restart deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n platform
- Scale: kubectl scale deployment/<name> --replicas=<N> -n platform
- Temporarily disable feature flag: curl -X PATCH https://config-service.internal/api/v1/flags/<flag> -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"enabled":false}'

On-call escalation policy (summary):
- P1: page platform-oncall (primary). If not acknowledged in 5 minutes, page secondary (PagerDuty automatically escalates at 5m). If unresolved after 30 minutes, escalate to eng-platform lead (Avery Chen) and notify product and reliability.
- P2: page platform-oncall; if not acknowledged in 15 minutes escalate to secondary.

Incident retrospective template (use for all P1 incidents):
- Title / Incident ID
- Timeline (with timestamps)
- Root cause
- Contributing factors
- Mitigations applied during the incident
- Postmortem actions (owner, due date, status)
- Rollout / verification plan for fixes

Recent retrospectives (summary):
- 2025-12-04 — High telemetry-ingest lag during midnight GC window: root cause was consumer JVM settings + sudden traffic shift from nightly jobs. Actions: bump consumer heap X -> Y, add JVM flags -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200, and add autoscaling policy for consumer group; owner: Priya Nair; ETA: 2026-01-10 (done).
- 2026-01-22 — platform-api regression after model roll: root cause: unexpected spike in KV cache misses due to version mismatch. Actions: add canary validation step to rollout pipeline, add cache-miss rate alert, ownership: Diego Morales, ETA: 2026-02-12 (in progress).

Platform roadmap (12–18 months, high level):
- Q2–Q3 2026: Observability rewrite — migrate from bespoke metrics pipeline to unified telemetry pipeline (owner: telemetry-team). Milestones: data model v1 (2026-06-15), rollout 50% (2026-08-01).
- Q3–Q4 2026: Runtime resilience features — improved autoscaling for GPU pools, graceful node eviction (owner: eng-infra). Milestones: autoscaler v2 alpha (2026-09-15).
- Q4 2026–Q1 2027: Cost & batching optimization — rollout intelligent batching heuristics and per-route cost analytics (owner: infra-economics).
- Ongoing: Runbook hygiene and noise reduction effort (quarterly).

How-tos and developer guidance (links and templates):
- New service onboarding checklist: produce an SLO doc, add Grafana dashboard, create 4 baseline alerts (error rate, latency, saturation, healthcheck), add runbook entry, assign on-call reviewer.
- Dashboard template: include top-line SLO, error budget burn, request rate, latency percentiles, backend error types, and infra metrics.
- Alert tuning steps: start wide thresholds, iterate using incident/false-positive rate, track alerts in a shared spreadsheet before promotion to paging.

Standards and conventions (applies to all platform services):
- Logging: structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, service, level, request_id, user_id (if applicable), error_code.
- Tracing: include traceparent header; spans for request ingress, model call, downstream call.
- Metrics: use telemetry metric names prefixed with service.<service>.<metric> and include cardinality controls.

Templates and artifacts (links):
- Incident postmortem template (use for all P1/P2): /confluence/eng-platform/templates/incident-postmortem
- New service onboarding checklist: /confluence/eng-platform/templates/onboarding-checklist
- Dashboard & alert template: /confluence/eng-platform/templates/dashboard-alert-template

Open action items (as of last update):
- [A-101] Complete canary validation step in rollout pipeline — owner: Diego Morales — due 2026-02-28 (in progress).
- [A-102] Finalize telemetry ingestion retention plan (60/30/7 days) — owner: Priya Nair — due 2026-03-15.
- [A-103] Reduce console-web paged alerts by 50% through better 5xx categorization — owner: Lena Park — due 2026-04-01.

Appendix: sample alert rule (prometheus-style)
- platform_api_5xx_rate: |
  sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\"}[5m])) > 0.005

Notes and references:
- See related playbooks in the team wiki and platform runbook collection. Keep this page updated when runbooks change and link any incident postmortem pages to this document.
- For private deployment differences (on-prem/VPC): consult eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures and the onprem-packaging runbooks for network and KMS considerations.

Document maintenance:
- Responsible owner: eng-platform (Avery Chen). Quarterly review cadence and after every P1 incident.
- Change process: raise a doc PR in the docs repo, add reviewers, and publish once at least two reviewers approve.
